dhp76:1: Should one see, as it were, a revealer of hidden treasures, one who points out what should be avoided,
dhp76:3: Who administers reproof where there is occasion for reproof, a man of intelligence, one should follow so wise a man;
dhp76:5: It will be better, not worse, for one to follow so wise a man.
dhp77:1: Let a man admonish and instruct, and forbid what is improper;
dhp77:3: For if he do so, he will be loved by the good, but hated by the wicked.
dhp78:1: One should not cultivate the friendship of evildoers; one should not cultivate fellows of the baser sort.
dhp78:3: Cultivate the friendship of men that are good, cultivate the best of men.
dhp79:1: He that drinks the Law sleeps happily, with mind serene;
dhp79:3: The wise man ever delights in the Law as taught by holy men.
dhp80:1: Ditch-diggers lead the water, arrow-makers straighten their shafts,
dhp80:3: Carpenters straighten the wood; wise men control themselves.
dhp81:1: Even as a solid rock is not moved by the wind,
dhp81:3: So wise men are not stirred by blame or praise.
dhp82:1: Even as a lake, deep, limpid, clear,
dhp82:3: So do wise men become calm after listening to the laws.
dhp83:1: Everywhere good men practice renunciation; good men talk not as if given to sensual pleasure;
dhp83:3: Wise men, touched either by happiness or by sorrow, show no change.
dhp84:1: Not for his own sake, not for the sake of another, should a man desire son or wealth or kingdom;
dhp84:3: He should not seek to gain success for himself by unjust means; so will he be upright, wise, and righteous.
dhp85:1: Of all men there are few that go to the other shore;
dhp85:3: The rest of mankind merely run up and down the bank.
dhp86:1: But those who conform to the Law, when the Law is rightly preached,
dhp86:3: Those men will cross to the farther shore of the Kingdom of Death, hard to cross though it be.
dhp87:1: Abandoning the dark state, the wise man should adopt the bright state.
dhp87:3: Leaving home, he should go forth to the homeless life. In solitude, where enjoyment is hard to find,
dhp88:1: There he should seek enjoyment, by forsaking the lusts of the flesh, with nothing he may call his own;
dhp88:3: The wise man should rid himself of the impurities of the heart.
dhp89:1: Those whose minds have been well trained in the Seven Elements of Knowledge,
dhp89:3: Those who have freed themselves from Attachment, and rejoice in that freedom,
dhp89:5: Those who have rid themselves of the Contaminations, and are full of light, they have passed into Nibbāna, even in this world.
